Patient-reported symptoms:
  Triggers: Olfactory (Smell): Related smells, Moral Violation: People misbehaving, Relationship Reminders: When people say things like my ex
  Maladaptive Strategies: Stay Near Exit: make sure to stay close to exit, Avoid Evaluation: Situations in which other people evaluate me / my appearance / my performance, Concealing Clothing: wear concealing clothing to avoid being noticed
  Threat: Avoid Unfamiliar Places: I avoid going to unfamiliar places because I cannot assess the danger, Threat in Movements: Sudden movements by others put me immediately on guard, Body on Alert: My body feels constantly tense and ready to react to danger
  Negative Appraisals: Self-Comparison: Somebody else would not have gotten into this situation, Lost Happiness: I used to be a happy person but now I am always miserable., Humiliation: I feel permanently humiliated by what happened

Vignette:
Rami, a 22-year-old auditor, had always been someone who found comfort in structure and predictability. He grew up in a close-knit Middle Eastern family, where values such as honor and resilience were deeply ingrained. Yet, these very principles were now at constant odds with the turmoil that had taken root within him following a traumatic incident that shattered his sense of safety and self-worth. 

The memory of that night loomed over him like a dark cloud, lingering vividly in his mind. Rami had been out with friends at a local bar, a place he had frequented without a second thought. The laughter and music had initially enveloped him in a sense of belonging, but that warmth quickly turned cold when he found himself alone with someone he thought he could trust. The violation he endured that night was not just physical; it stripped away layers of his identity, leaving him feeling exposed and vulnerable. 

In the months that followed, Rami had become acutely aware of the world around him, particularly the smells that seemed innocuous to others. The scent of cheap cologne, reminiscent of the perpetrator, would hit him unexpectedly, sending him spiraling back to that night. He found himself avoiding places where he might encounter reminders, both big and small. Even the faint odor of alcohol would trigger a rush of anxiety, forcing him to retreat into the safety of familiar spaces. 

His daily life began to take on a different rhythm, one marked by heightened vigilance and a growing sense of isolation. At work, Rami started to feel the weight of scrutiny in ways he had never before experienced. He would stay near the exit during meetings, a habit formed from his need to escape at a moment’s notice. The thought of being evaluated—whether it was his performance on an audit or even the way he looked—became unbearable. He wore baggy, concealing clothing, hoping to blend into the background, a desperate attempt to shield himself from unwanted attention. 

Rami’s body was in a constant state of alert. He could feel tension coursing through his muscles, always ready to react to the slightest perceived threat. Sudden movements from colleagues in the office would send his heart racing, a visceral reminder of the unpredictability that had shattered his sense of control. He had come to believe that his ability to navigate the world had been irrevocably altered; he avoided unfamiliar places, convinced that he could not assess the dangers that lurked there. The very thought of venturing into the unknown filled him with dread.

As the weeks turned into months, Rami's internal monologue shifted. He would catch himself comparing his situation to those of others, entrenched in a belief that someone else would not have found themselves in such a predicament. This negative appraisal deepened his sense of humiliation, making him feel as though he were forever marked by the trauma. He had once been a carefree person, but now he felt like a shadow of his former self, weighed down by an unshakeable misery. 

The isolation grew unbearable; friends began to notice his absence from social gatherings, but Rami found excuses to avoid interactions that might expose him to even the slightest chance of vulnerability. He felt he could no longer share the joys of life when he was constantly reminded of his own suffering. 

What finally brought Rami to seek help was a particularly poignant moment. One afternoon, while auditing a new client, he overheard a colleague mention their ex in a conversation. The words struck him like a physical blow, triggering a rush of emotions that left him feeling disoriented. In that moment, he realized he was no longer able to manage the weight of his past alone. 

As he sat in the waiting room of the clinic, anxiety coursed through him. What frightened him most was the fear of being judged, of not being understood. Yet, beneath the fear lay a flicker of hope: the possibility that, perhaps, he could reclaim the happiness he had lost. Rami was ready to confront the shadows that had taken hold of his life, yearning for a path forward that would allow him to rediscover who he once was.
